newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: ENKA offers Yugo firms cooperation - paper.
newsitem.headline: ENKA offers Yugo firms cooperation - paper.

text.p: Turkey's Enka Holding is interested in taking part in infrastructure projects in Yugoslavia and helping obtain credits for their financing, Belgrade newspaper Borba said on Monday.

"I am interested in working on any infrastructure facility in Yugoslavia, and in helping obtain credits for any large projects," Shariq Tarre, owner of the Turkish construction firm, was quoted by Borba as saying.
Tarre said his company was ready to participate in the construction of roads in Yugoslavia, to enter joint ventures with Yugoslav firms and cooperate on third markets.
Yugoslav builders know the world market well, especially Africa and Russia, and the two sides can cooperate on various projects, from highways to electric power plants, Tarre said.
The two sides could work on a fifty-fifty principle, Tarre said, adding that Enka had good relations with international financial organisations and business ties in Japan and the United States.
He said later this year, probably in August, Enka would begin building a highway in Croatia from Croatia's border with Slovenia, via Zagreb and Sisak, to its border with Bosnia-Herzegovina.
